newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Trade looks for new highs in Railtrack.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Trade looks for new highs in Railtrack.

text.p: A relatively big buyer of call options in Railtrack shares -- already up about 17.5 percent in the last two weeks -- appears to be betting on a further advance in the stock next week, options dealers said.
Five hundred September 280 calls were purchased at 4p. Dealers said they believe the calls were bought outright.
That means the shares must rise above 284p before the September expiry on September 18 for the trade to be profitable.
"It looks like a cheap way to get into the stock," said one dealer of the trade.
By 1338 GMT, Railtrack shares were up 7-1/2p to 277-1/2p, after rising to a new peak at 300p.
Railtrack shares have been bolstered in recently by talk that a U.S. buyer is building a stake in the company. Marketmakers noted talk of a big UK buyer today.
"Last week, it was alleged talk of an American buyer. Today, it's talk of a domestic buyer," said one marketmaker.
Trading volume in the underlying shares was heavy at 11.9 million at 1338 GMT, making Railtrack shares among the most actively traded in London.
Elsewhere, dealers noted the sale of 1,000 September 200p straddles at 5p in British Gas shares.
"They're betting the stock won't move much," said another dealer."A lot of the news is already out."
Shares in British Gas were up 1p to 200p after the company reported an expected drop in its half-year profits.

British Gas also said it was closer to regulator Ofgas on a review of its domestic price controls than on a parallel review of its Transco over a dispute over transmission operations. It said it expects the price review to be settled by the end of September or middle of October.
